body.statement: For each \(d<T\), there is a positive function \(u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})\), with \(b_d=\min\{T,d+2\}\), such that \(g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})=u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})\prod_{t=b_d+1}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})\). Consequently, for \(b_d\le k<\ell\le T\), \(P(X_\ell\mid X_k,W,A,D=d)=K_{k+1}\cdots K_\ell\).
body.justification: The factorization turns nonconsecutive audit measurements into legal composed transition kernels and bounds every local elimination state by an interval frontier.
body.gap: The passive monotone results normalize response kernels; they do not exploit a substantive Markov suffix observed through partial audits.
body.consumer: The interval-block calculus uses this lemma to transport an identified boundary marginal to the endpoint without recovering the missing trajectory.
